threads.body: [General] `TracingListView` inherits `AbstractList` operations such as `contains`, `indexOf`, and `clear`, which consume this tracing iterator internally. Several of those operations return early or iterate a fixed count without a final `hasNext()`, so they create process telemetry even though no message-processing callback ran and can leave the last `ProcessingInvocation` scope current (for example, `response.getMessages().subList(...).contains(firstMessage)` or `.clear()`). Delegate non-processing list operations directly, as the existing `get`/`set`/`add`/`remove` overrides do, rather than letting `AbstractList` route them through the tracing iterator.

[General] Marking a sublist currently flips `tracingList.processingOwnedOutsideSqsSdk`, so ownership is stored on the entire response rather than on the concrete view. If a framework is handed only `response.getMessages().subList(0, 1)`, a later raw traversal of the parent or a sibling view also sees this flag and emits no fallback Process span, even though that work was never handed off. Keep ownership scoped to the exact list/view and have each traversal wrapper consult that scope so unrelated messages remain visible.

[General] `ReceiveMessageResult.toString()` appends `getMessages()`, and the inherited list `toString()` obtains this overridden iterator. Simply logging a response therefore emits one Process span per message; with the removal of `firstIterator`, every log call now does so. Non-processing object methods (at minimum `toString()`, plus `equals()`/`hashCode()` where they iterate on supported JDKs) need an untraced implementation.

This issue also appears on line 265 of the same file.

threads.body: [General] This documentation says ownership applies to a list “and its views,” but the implementation gives every `TracingListView` independent ownership, and `parentProcessingOwnershipDoesNotDisableListView` explicitly verifies that marking the parent does not suppress a view. Describe the exact-object behavior so framework callers do not incorrectly assume ownership propagates to subsequently created views.
